subject: headcrab
label: headcrab.mdl, in the place of the game's models/headcrab.mdl

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's words: a low body with four legs splayed out, a beak below, and the long-to-high ratio (25.5 by 13). In the front, side, back and top views the legs stick out past the body and the beak hangs below it, with nothing extra sticking out.

M2.reason: Measured length 25.5 against the brief's 26 is within 2%, and height 13 against 13 is exact. Width (21.6) is not a brief figure, so it is not scored.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: (1) four clawed legs: four legs are present, all tapered spikes in the top and below views; (2) sharp front claws: no separate claws are visible. The front pair is the same spike as the others, and the front-left and back-left views show no claw shape at any leg tip. Missing small part, so at most 1. (3) beak-like mouth underneath: a yellow cone hangs centre-under the body, visible in the front, back and below views; present. Only the claws are missing, and that caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: Body is an even tan matching the brief's fleshy tan; the beak is a yellow cone. Colour matches the brief's words, and the material reads as one matte skin-like surface, not glossy metal.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings. The surface is plain with soft fan-shaped facet shading on the top and no stray marks or wear, so nothing is added wrong.

M6.reason: In the line-up, the asset (B) is a flat-shaded, untextured dome with straight spikes and a yellow cone. Beside Half-Life's chumtoad, roach and leech, it looks like a stand-in model: no skin texture, no eye or mouth detail, and a turtle or beetle read rather than a headcrab. A player would not take it for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The mouth cone sits underneath and forward, as the brief describes (front and below views). The dome stands upright on its legs, with the cone pointing down and forward. The brief gives no original facing to compare against, so this is judged from the brief's words alone.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 288 triangles it is under the median of Half-Life's kind (308) and well under twice that, so it passes the triangle limit. The legs and beak join the body in every view, with no open, inside-out or floating part visible.
